name: Norman Rockwell
hook: The Saturday Evening Post illustrator whose Four Freedoms and Rosie define mid-century America.

facts.label: Saturday Evening Post covers
facts.statement: Rockwell created his first Saturday Evening Post cover in 1916 and went on to paint more than 300 for the magazine.

facts.label: Triple Self-Portrait
facts.statement: His Triple Self-Portrait graced the Post cover of February 13, 1960, and appeared on a 29-cent stamp in 1994.

facts.label: the Four Freedoms
facts.statement: Rockwell's Four Freedoms paintings, inspired by FDR's 1941 speech, promoted war bonds; Freedom from Want shows a Thanksgiving turkey.

facts.label: Rosie the Riveter
facts.statement: For a 1943 Post cover, Rockwell used a Vermont phone operator as the model for Rosie the Riveter.

facts.label: A Christmas Carol
facts.statement: Fond of Dickens and Victorian images, Rockwell based a painting in the Stockbridge museum on A Christmas Carol.

facts.label: Ruby Bridges
facts.statement: Rockwell painted Ruby Bridges, who in 1960 made history by integrating an all-white school in New Orleans.
